`[Supported fact]` The SQL function `load_extension()` loads an SQLite extension, but extension loading is disabled by default and must first be enabled with `sqlite3_enable_load_extension()`. (https://sqlite.org/lang_corefunc.html)

`[Inference]` Because FTS5 can be either compiled in or provided as a loadable extension, compile-option checks tell you whether the current SQLite library was built with `SQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5`, but they do not by themselves prove that FTS5 is currently registered on a specific connection. `PRAGMA module_list` is the stronger documented connection-level check. (https://sqlite.org/compile.html , https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html , https://sqlite.org/lang_corefunc.html , https://sqlite.org/pragma.html)

**External-Content FTS5 Tables**

`[Supported fact]` An external-content FTS5 table is created by setting `content=` to the name of a table, virtual table, or view in the same database; `content_rowid=` can override the default rowid column name used by FTS5. (https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html)

`[Supported fact]` When FTS5 needs column values from an external-content table, it queries the content object by rowid, and it may also query it ordered ascending or descending by the content rowid. (https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html)

`[Supported fact]` With external content, “all FTS5 functionality may be used,” but the user is responsible for keeping the full-text index consistent with the content object; if not, query results may be unpredictable. (https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html)

`[Supported fact]` If a query against the external-content FTS5 table does not use the full-text index, such as one without `MATCH` or equivalent table-valued-function syntax, SQLite effectively passes that query through to the content table, so the FTS index does not affect the result. (https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html)

`[Supported fact]` If a query does use the full-text index, FTS5 first gets matching rowids from the index and then looks up the corresponding column values in the content table. (https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html)

`[Supported fact]` Triggers are one documented way to keep an external-content FTS5 table synchronized with its content table. (https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html)

`[Supported fact]` Creating those triggers after the content table already contains rows does not backfill the FTS index; the triggers only keep later inserts, updates, and deletes synchronized. (https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html)

`[Supported fact]` If the FTS index and content table become inconsistent, the documented `rebuild` command can discard the existing FTS index and rebuild it from the current content table. (https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html)

`[Supported fact]` External-content FTS5 tables do not support `REPLACE` conflict handling; operations that specify `REPLACE` are handled using `ABORT`. (https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html)

**Uncertainty / Lack Of Good Evidence**

`[Lack of good evidence]` In the primary SQLite pages I reviewed, I did not find a dedicated single-purpose API documented as “detect whether FTS5 is available now on this connection” beyond the general mechanisms above: registered-module introspection (`PRAGMA module_list`), compile-option introspection, and extension loading.

# PRAGMA compile_options

## Purpose

`PRAGMA compile_options` returns the names of [compile-time options](https://www.sqlite.org/compile.html) used when building SQLite, one option per row. The "SQLITE_" prefix is omitted from the returned option names.

## Usage

### Basic Syntax

```sql
PRAGMA compile_options;
```

### Example Output

When executed, this pragma returns a result set with one row per compile-time option. For example:

```
THREADSAFE
HAVE_ISNAN
SOUNDEX
...
```

## How It's Used to Detect Features

Since compile-time options control which features are compiled into SQLite, you can use this pragma to:

1. **Query available features** - Check if a specific feature was enabled at compile time
2. **Detect build capabilities** - Determine what functionality is available in your SQLite installation
3. **Conditional logic** - Adjust application behavior based on available features

### Example Detection Query

```sql
SELECT compile_options FROM pragma_compile_options() 
WHERE compile_options LIKE '%THREADSAFE%';
```

Or as a simple query:

```sql
PRAGMA compile_options;
```

Then check the result set for options like:
- `THREADSAFE` - Thread safety support
- `ENABLE_FTS5` - Full-text search
- `ENABLE_JSON1` - JSON support
- `OMIT_DEPRECATED` - Whether deprecated features are included

## Related Interfaces

- **C/C++ API**: [`sqlite3_compileoption_get()`](https://www.sqlite.org/c3ref/compileoption_get.html)
- **SQL Function**: `sqlite_compileoption_get()` SQL function

This pragma provides a portable way to detect SQLite's capabilities at runtime.

# FTS5 Detection and External Content Tables

## 1. Detecting FTS5 Availability

### Compile-Time Detection

**Method: Check SQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5 preprocessor symbol**

FTS5 is included in SQLite since version 3.9.0 (2015-10-14). To enable it at compile time:

> "If using the canonical source tree, FTS5 is enabled by specifying the "--enable-fts5" option when running the configure script. (FTS5 is currently disabled by default for the source-tree configure script and enabled by default for the amalgamation configure script, but these defaults might change in the future.) Or, if sqlite3.c is compiled using some other build system, by arranging for the SQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5 pre-processor symbol to be defined."

### Runtime Detection

**Method 1: Use the fts5() function**

The fts5() SQL function can be invoked to obtain the fts5_api pointer:

```c
fts5_api *fts5_api_from_db(sqlite3 *db){
  fts5_api *pRet = 0;
  sqlite3_stmt *pStmt = 0;

  if( SQLITE_OK==sqlite3_prepare(db, "SELECT fts5(?1)", -1, &pStmt, 0) ){
    sqlite3_bind_pointer(pStmt, 1, (void*)&pRet, "fts5_api_ptr", NULL);
    sqlite3_step(pStmt);
  }
  sqlite3_finalize(pStmt);
  return pRet;
}
```

If the fts5() function doesn't exist or returns NULL, FTS5 is unavailable.

**Method 2: PRAGMA compile_options**

Query available compile-time options:
```sql
PRAGMA compile_options;
```

If "ENABLE_FTS5" appears in the results, FTS5 is enabled.

---

## 2. External Content Tables

### Overview and Options

External content FTS5 tables store only full-text index entries, not the actual column data. The original content is retrieved from a separate "content table" as needed.

> "The 'content' option may be used to create an FTS5 table that stores only FTS full-text index entries. Because the column values themselves are usually much larger than the associated full-text index entries, this can save significant database space."

### Creating External Content Tables

# SQLite Compilation Options Diagnostics

## C Functions

**sqlite3_compileoption_used()**
> "returns 0 or 1 indicating whether the specified option was defined at compile time. The SQLITE_ prefix may be omitted from the option name passed to sqlite3_compileoption_used()."

**sqlite3_compileoption_get()**
> "allows iterating over the list of options that were defined at compile time by returning the N-th compile time option string. If N is out of range, sqlite3_compileoption_get() returns a NULL pointer. The SQLITE_ prefix is omitted from any strings returned by sqlite3_compileoption_get()."

## SQL Functions

Corresponding SQL functions `sqlite_compileoption_used()` and `sqlite_compileoption_get()` provide equivalent functionality at the SQL level.

## SQLITE_OMIT_COMPILEOPTION_DIAGS Caveat

> "Support for the diagnostic functions sqlite3_compileoption_used() and sqlite3_compileoption_get() may be omitted by specifying the SQLITE_OMIT_COMPILEOPTION_DIAGS option at compile time."

When this compile-time option is specified:
- `sqlite3_compileoption_used()` is defined to return `0`
- `sqlite3_compileoption_get()` is defined to return `((void*)0)` (NULL)

This allows eliminating the diagnostic functionality entirely for stripped-down SQLite builds.

# SQLite FTS5 Extension - Key Sections

## Compiling and Using FTS5

### 2.1. Building FTS5 as part of SQLite

As of [version 3.9.0](releaselog/3_9_0.html) (2015-10-14), FTS5 is included as part of the SQLite [amalgamation](amalgamation.html). If using the canonical source tree, FTS5 is enabled by specifying the "--enable-fts5" option when running the configure script. (FTS5 is currently disabled by default for the source-tree configure script and enabled by default for the amalgamation configure script, but these defaults might change in the future.)

Or, if sqlite3.c is compiled using some other build system, by arranging for the SQLITE\_ENABLE\_FTS5 pre-processor symbol to be defined.

### 2.2. Building a Loadable Extension

Alternatively, FTS5 may be built as a loadable extension.

The canonical FTS5 source code consists of a series of \*.c and other files in the "ext/fts5" directory of the SQLite source tree. A build process reduces this to just two files - "fts5.c" and "fts5.h" - which may be used to build an SQLite loadable extension.

1.  Obtain the latest SQLite code from fossil.
2.  Create a Makefile as described in [How To Compile SQLite](howtocompile.html).
3.  Build the "fts5.c" target, which also creates fts5.h.

$ wget -c https://sqlite.org/src/tarball/SQLite-trunk.tgz?uuid=trunk -O SQLite-trunk.tgz
.... output ...
$ tar -xzf SQLite-trunk.tgz
$ cd SQLite-trunk
$ ./configure && make fts5.c
... lots of output ...
$ ls fts5.\[ch\]
fts5.c        fts5.h

The code in "fts5.c" may then be compiled into a loadable extension or statically linked into an application as described in [Compiling Loadable Extensions](loadext.html#build). There are two entry points defined, both of which do the same thing:

*   sqlite3\_fts\_init
*   sqlite3\_fts5\_init

The other file, "fts5.h", is not required to compile the FTS5 extension. It is used by applications that implement [custom FTS5 tokenizers or auxiliary functions](fts5.html#extending_fts5).

# SQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5 and Compile-Time Options Reporting

## SQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5

According to the documentation:

> **SQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5**
> 
> When this option is defined in the [amalgamation](amalgamation.html), version 5 of the full-text search engine ([fts5](fts5.html)) is added to the build automatically.

## Compile-Time Options Reporting

The documentation states in the Overview section:

> The [compile_options pragma](pragma.html#pragma_compile_options) can be used to determine which of the options listed below were used in building a given copy of SQLite.

However, the documentation does **not** explicitly specify:
- Whether only options with the `SQLITE_` prefix are reported
- Whether some options are omitted from reporting
- Any limitations on what appears in the `compile_options` pragma output

The documentation references both `sqlite3_compileoption_used()` and `sqlite3_compileoption_get()` C/C++ functions in the context of [SQLITE_OMIT_COMPILEOPTION_DIAGS](compile.html#omit_compileoption_diags), which can be used to omit the entire compile-time option diagnostics feature, but does not detail which specific options are or are not included in the reporting.

# Relevant Sections from SQLite FTS5 Documentation

## Section 6.3. The 'delete' Command

This command is only available with [external content](fts5.html#external_content_tables) and [contentless](fts5.html#contentless_tables) tables. It is used to delete the index entries associated with a single row from the full-text index. This command and the [delete-all](fts5.html#the_delete_all_command) command are the only ways to remove entries from the full-text index of a contentless table.

In order to use this command to delete a row, the text value 'delete' must be inserted into the special column with the same name as the table. The rowid of the row to delete is inserted into the rowid column. The values inserted into the other columns must match the values currently stored in the table. For example:

```sql
-- Insert a row with rowid=14 into the fts5 table.
INSERT INTO ft(rowid, a, b, c) VALUES(14, $a, $b, $c);

-- Remove the same row from the fts5 table.
INSERT INTO ft(ft, rowid, a, b, c) VALUES('delete', 14, $a, $b, $c);
```

If the values "inserted" into the text columns as part of a 'delete' command are not the same as those currently stored within the table, the results may be unpredictable.

The reason for this is easy to understand: When a document is inserted into the FTS5 table, an entry is added to the full-text index to record the position of each token within the new document. When a document is removed, the original data is required in order to determine the set of entries that need to be removed from the full-text index. So if the data supplied to FTS5 when a row is deleted using this command is different from that used to determine the set of token instances when it was inserted, some full-text index entries may not be correctly deleted, or FTS5 may try to remove index entries that do not exist. This can leave the full-text index in an unpredictable state, making future query results unreliable.

## Section 6.4. The 'delete-all' Command

# Détecter FTS5 à l'exécution et travailler avec les tables « external content » FTS5

## 1. Statut de FTS5 dans les builds SQLite (fait documenté)

Depuis la **version 3.9.0 (2015-10-14), FTS5 fait partie de l'amalgamation SQLite**. Dans l'arbre source canonique, il s'active avec `--enable-fts5` ; avec un autre système de build, en définissant le symbole préprocesseur `SQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5`. La doc précise que « FTS5 is currently disabled by default for the source-tree configure script and enabled by default for the amalgamation configure script, **but these defaults might change in the future** » ([fts5.html §2.1](https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html)). La page des options de compilation confirme : « When this option is defined in the amalgamation, version 5 of the full-text search engine (fts5) is added to the build automatically » ([compile.html](https://www.sqlite.org/compile.html)).

FTS5 peut aussi être construit comme **extension chargeable** (fichiers `fts5.c`/`fts5.h`), avec deux points d'entrée : `sqlite3_fts_init` et `sqlite3_fts5_init` ([fts5.html §2.2](https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html)).

## 2. Méthodes de détection

### a) `PRAGMA compile_options` (fait)

Ce pragma « returns the names of compile-time options used when building SQLite, one option per row. The "SQLITE_" prefix is omitted from the returned option names » ([pragma.html#pragma_compile_options](https://www.sqlite.org/pragma.html#pragma_compile_options)). La page compile.html indique explicitement : « The compile_options pragma can be used to determine which of the options listed below were used in building a given copy of SQLite » ([compile.html](https://www.sqlite.org/compile.html)).

En pratique, on cherche donc la ligne `ENABLE_FTS5` (sans le préfixe `SQLITE_`).

### b) `sqlite_compileoption_used()` / `sqlite3_compileoption_used()` (fait)

`sqlite3_compileoption_used()` « returns 0 or 1 indicating whether the specified option was defined at compile time. The SQLITE_ prefix may be omitted from the option name ». Des fonctions SQL correspondantes `sqlite_compileoption_used()` et `sqlite_compileoption_get()` existent ([c3ref/compileoption_get.html](https://www.sqlite.org/c3ref/compileoption_get.html)).

**Limitation documentée** : ces diagnostics peuvent être supprimés via `SQLITE_OMIT_COMPILEOPTION_DIAGS`, auquel cas `sqlite3_compileoption_used()` est défini pour renvoyer `0` et `sqlite3_compileoption_get()` pour renvoyer `NULL` (même source). Donc un `0` ne prouve pas l'absence de FTS5.

### c) Fonction SQL `fts5()` (fait, mais usage précis)

La doc décrit `fts5()` comme le moyen d'obtenir le pointeur `fts5_api` : « the application invokes the SQL user-defined function fts5() with a single argument […] set to a pointer to a pointer to an fts5_api object using the sqlite3_bind_pointer() interface », avec l'exemple `fts5_api_from_db()` ([fts5.html, section « Extending FTS5 »](https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html)). Avertissement de compatibilité documenté : « Prior to SQLite version 3.20.0 (2017-08-01), the fts5() worked slightly differently. »

> **Inférence (non affirmée telle quelle par la doc)** : puisque `fts5()` n'est enregistrée que si l'extension FTS5 est présente sur la connexion, l'échec de `SELECT fts5(?1)` (ou un retour `NULL`) indique l'indisponibilité de FTS5. La doc présente cette fonction comme un mécanisme d'extension, **pas** comme un test de détection officiel.

### d) Test empirique par création de table (inférence)

> **Inférence, non documentée comme telle** : le test le plus fiable reste de tenter `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE temp.x USING fts5(a);` et d'intercepter l'erreur. Je n'ai pas trouvé de page SQLite primaire recommandant explicitement cette technique — je la signale comme pratique courante, pas comme fait documenté.

**Recommandation** : combiner (a)/(b) pour le diagnostic informatif et (d) pour la décision réelle, car `compile_options` reflète les options de compilation, pas l'état de la connexion.

> **Incertitude explicite** : la documentation consultée **ne dit pas** si `PRAGMA compile_options` liste `ENABLE_FTS5` lorsque FTS5 est chargé comme extension chargeable à l'exécution. Logiquement il ne devrait pas (l'option n'a pas été définie lors de la compilation du cœur), mais je n'ai pas de source primaire l'affirmant. C'est la raison principale de préférer un test fonctionnel.

Aucune fonction du type `fts5_version()` n'apparaît dans la documentation FTS5 — ne comptez pas dessus.

## 3. Tables « external content » : garanties et limites

### Principe (fait)

« The "content" option may be used to create an FTS5 table that stores only FTS full-text index entries. Because the column values themselves are usually much larger than the associated full-text index entries, this can save significant database space. » En mode external content, on donne à `content=` « the name of a database object (table, virtual table or view) that may be queried by FTS5 at any time to retrieve the column values » ; alors « **all FTS5 functionality may be used, but it is the responsibility of the user to ensure that the contents of the full-text index are consistent** with the named database object. If they are not, query results may be unpredictable » ([fts5.html §4.4](https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html)).

Requêtes émises par FTS5 vers la table de contenu (fait, §4.4.3) :

```sql
SELECT <content_rowid>, <cols> FROM <content> WHERE <content_rowid> = ?;
SELECT <content_rowid>, <cols> FROM <content> ORDER BY <content_rowid> ASC;   -- ou DESC
```

`<content_rowid>` vaut littéralement `rowid` par défaut, ou la valeur de l'option `content_rowid=`.

### Ce qui est garanti

- Toutes les colonnes sont lisibles (contrairement aux tables contentless) — §4.4.
- La commande `'rebuild'` : « This command first deletes the entire full-text index, then rebuilds it based on the contents of the table or content table. **It is not available with contentless tables** » ([fts5.html §6.12](https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html)). C'est le remède officiel à toute incohérence.
- Les commandes `'delete'` et `'delete-all'` sont disponibles pour les tables external content et contentless (§6.3, §6.4).

### Ce qui n'est PAS garanti (limitations documentées)

1. **Aucune synchronisation automatique.** « It is still the responsibility of the user to ensure that the contents of an external content FTS5 table are kept up to date with the content table. » La doc propose des triggers `AFTER INSERT/DELETE/UPDATE` (§4.4.3).

2. **`REPLACE` non supporté.** « Like contentless tables, external content tables do not support REPLACE conflict handling. Any operations that specify REPLACE conflict handling are handled using **ABORT**. » (§4.4.3)

3. **Sémantique scindée des requêtes** (§4.4.4) : sans `MATCH` (ni syntaxe de fonction table), « the query is effectively passed through to the external content table » et l'index FTS n'a aucun effet ; avec `MATCH`, l'index fournit les rowids puis les valeurs sont relues dans la table de contenu. D'où les deux exemples documentés d'incohérence : `SELECT * FROM ft` renvoie 2 lignes tandis que `ft('gold')` en renvoie 0 ; ou l'inverse, `ft('gold')` renvoyant une ligne dont la colonne `t` est **NULL** parce qu'aucune donnée correspondante n'existe dans `t1`.

4. **Les triggers ne rattrapent pas l'existant.** « creating the triggers does not copy existing rows from the content table into the FTS index. The triggers are only able to ensure that updates made to the content table **after they are created** are reflected in the FTS index. » (§4.4.4) → il faut un `'rebuild'` initial.

5. **Ordre des opérations impératif sur DELETE/UPDATE** (§4.4.4.1) : lors d'un DELETE, FTS5 relit les valeurs courantes dans la table de contenu pour les retokeniser et savoir quelles entrées supprimer. « If the retrieved values do not match the set of entries in the FTS index for the row, then some tokens may be left in the FTS index, leading to inconsistent query results later on. » Conséquence : « **to delete a row from both the content table and the FTS5 external content table, the FTS5 table must be updated first** (so that the content table row is still available to it). » Idem pour UPDATE, implémenté comme DELETE + INSERT.

6. **La commande `'delete'` exige les valeurs exactes** : « The values inserted into the other columns must match the values currently stored in the table. […] If the values "inserted" […] are not the same as those currently stored within the table, the results may be **unpredictable** » (§6.3). C'est précisément pourquoi les triggers d'exemple utilisent `old.*`.

7. **`'integrity-check'` est plus faible par défaut** (§6.7) : les trois formes sont équivalentes pour les tables non-external-content, mais « For an external content table, the contents of the index are only compared to the contents of the external content table **if the value specified for the rank column is 1** ». Il faut donc explicitement :
   ```sql
   INSERT INTO ft(ft, rank) VALUES('integrity-check', 1);
   ```
   En cas d'écart, la commande échoue avec `SQLITE_CORRUPT_VTAB`.

8. **`'secure-delete'` verrouille le format de fichier** (§6.13) : une fois une ligne mise à jour/supprimée avec cette option, « the FTS5 table may no longer be read or written by any version of FTS5 earlier than 3.42.0 », erreur « invalid fts5 file format (found 5, expected 4) - run 'rebuild' ». Réversible via `'rebuild'` sous une version ≥ 3.42.0. Valeur par défaut : 0.

### Observation sur la documentation elle-même

La section **§4.4.4.1 est intitulée « Updates and Deletes on Contentless Tables »** alors que son contenu décrit explicitement le comportement des tables *external content* (elle parle de requêtes vers `<content>` et conclut sur « the FTS5 external content table »). Il s'agit vraisemblablement d'un titre imprécis dans la doc primaire ; le corps du texte est sans ambiguïté. Je le signale comme **observation**, pas comme fait établi par SQLite.

## 4. Points connexes utiles pour éviter la confusion

- **Contentless** (`content=''`) : pas d'UPDATE/DELETE, pas d'INSERT sans rowid non-NULL, pas de REPLACE, toute colonne autre que rowid lue renvoie NULL, `'rebuild'` indisponible (§4.4.1).
- **Contentless-delete** (`content='', contentless_delete=1`, depuis 3.43.0) : supporte DELETE, `INSERT OR REPLACE`, et UPDATE *seulement* si toutes les colonnes utilisateur reçoivent une nouvelle valeur ; ne supporte **pas** la commande `'delete'`. « Unless backwards compatibility is required, new code should prefer contentless-delete tables to contentless tables » (§4.4.2).
